Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant journey you've been on, becoming a new mother, and I'm here to support you in any way I can. As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool designed to help us understand how you're feeling and if there are any concerns that we should address together. The purpose of this assessment is to check in with you about your emotional well-being during this postpartum period, which can be a time of significant adjustment and change. Please know that everything we discuss is confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe and supportive space for you to express yourself honestly. 

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better picture of how you've been feeling over the past week. I'll ask you each question, and you can share your thoughts and feelings with me. We'll take it one question at a time, and there are no right or wrong answers. This is simply a way for us to have a more in-depth conversation about your emotional health and well-being.

Let's get started. The first question is about how you've been feeling over the past week. Have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things as much as you used to?

.. to be honest, not really. I mean, I still find some things funny, but it's just not the same as it used to be. I feel like I've been so caught up in taking care of the baby and trying to figure everything out that I haven't really had the energy or the mood to laugh like I used to. Sometimes I'll be playing with the baby or watching a funny video, and for a second, I'll feel a little bit of joy, but it's fleeting. It's like, I can see the funny side of things, but it's just not as enjoyable as it was before. And sometimes, even when I do laugh, I feel guilty, like I should be focusing on more serious things, like making sure the baby is okay. It's hard to explain, but it feels like my sense of humor has just been a little... muted, I guess, since having the baby. (pausing, looking down) Sorry, does that make sense.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(sighing) Yeah, that's not really me right now. I mean, like I said, I can still find some things funny, but it's just not the same. I feel like I've lost a little bit of myself, you know? I used to be the one who could always make my friends laugh, and now I just feel so... serious all the time. And it's not just that I'm not laughing as much, it's that I'm just not enjoying things as much as I used to. Even things that I used to love, like reading or watching my favorite TV shows, just don't seem as interesting to me anymore. (looking down, fidgeting with hands) It's like, I'm just going through the motions of taking care of the baby and trying to be a good mom, but I'm not really feeling anything. And when I do feel something, it's usually just anxiety or worry about the baby, or guilt about not being a good enough mom. (pausing, looking up) Sorry, I guess that's just how I'm feeling right now.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking head) Not really. I mean, I used to love planning things and looking forward to them, but now it just feels like so much work. Even things that I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or meeting a friend for coffee, just feel like too much effort now. And with the baby, it's hard to plan anything because you never know when they're going to need something or when they'll get fussy. (sighing) I feel like I'm just trying to get through each day, rather than actually looking forward to things. Sometimes I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, like going to a movie or trying a new restaurant, but then I'll just feel overwhelmed by all the things I need to do to make it happen, like finding a babysitter or making sure the baby's feedings are taken care of. (looking down) It's just easier to stay home and not bother, you know? (pausing, voice barely above a whisper) It's like, I've lost my sense of excitement and anticipation. Everything just feels so... heavy.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding) Yes... that sounds like me. I mean, I feel like I'm always wondering if I'm doing something wrong, or if I'm not doing enough for the baby. If the baby cries, I feel like it's because I'm not feeding them right, or because I'm not changing their diaper fast enough. And if I make a mistake, like forgetting to burp them or something, I feel like I'm the worst mom in the world. (looking down, voice filled with self-doubt) I just feel like I'm not good enough, and that I'm going to mess everything up. Even when my partner or family members try to reassure me, I just can't shake the feeling that I'm not doing things right. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's like, I know intellectually that everyone makes mistakes, and that it's okay not to be perfect, but emotionally... it's just hard for me to let go of that guilt and self-blame. (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) Sometimes I feel like I'm just waiting for someone to tell me that I'm doing everything wrong, and that I'm not cut out for this whole mom thing.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Yes, that's me all the time. I mean, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing their diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if the baby stops breathing? Or what if I forget to do something important? Or what if... (trailing off, looking anxious) It's just this constant stream of "what ifs" running through my head, and it's exhausting. And the worst part is, it's not even like I can control it. I'll be trying to relax, or watch TV, or take a shower, and these thoughts just pop into my head out of nowhere. (rubbing temples) It's like, I know they're not rational, but I just can't seem to shake them. And sometimes, it's not even just about the baby. I'll worry about my relationship with my partner, or about how I'm going to manage taking care of the baby and doing everything else I need to do. (sighing) It's just this constant feeling of being "on edge", you know? Like, I'm always waiting for something to go wrong, even when everything is fine. (looking up, eyes wide with anxiety) And it's hard to sleep, too. I'll lie awake at night, just thinking about all these worst-case scenarios, and it's like... (shaking head) I don't know, it's just really hard to turn it off.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(taking a deep breath) Yes... that's happened to me too. I'll be doing something normal, like feeding the baby or doing laundry, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to pass out or something. (shaking head) It's so scary, because it comes out of nowhere, and I don't know how to make it stop. Sometimes I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just feel like I'm not in control, like I'm just going to drop them or something. (wrapping arms around self) And it's not even like I'm thinking about anything scary, it's just this feeling of... ( searching for words) ...of overwhelm, I guess. Like, everything is just too much for me to handle. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) And sometimes, when it happens, I'll just start crying, because I don't know what to do. I'll feel like I'm losing my mind, or like I'm not a good mom. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's hard to explain, but it's just this feeling of being completely overwhelmed, and not knowing how to make it stop. (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) It's really scary, because I don't know when it's going to happen, or how to make it go away.
Things have been getting on top of me

(exhaling heavily) Oh, yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, and the house, and my relationship with my partner... it's just all so much. And sometimes, it feels like I'm drowning in it all. (looking down, shaking head) I'll be trying to do one thing, like feeding the baby, and then I'll think about all the other things I need to do, like laundry and dishes and grocery shopping... and it just feels like too much. (wrapping arms around self) I'll feel like I'm just trying to keep my head above water, but I'm not really getting anything done. And then I'll feel guilty, because I'm not doing enough, or I'm not doing it well enough. (sighing) It's just this constant feeling of being overwhelmed, and not knowing how to make it all work. (pausing, looking up) Sometimes, I'll just sit down, and I'll feel like I'm going to cry, because I just don't know how to do it all. (voice cracking) I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, and that if one more thing goes wrong, I'll just... (trailing off, struggling to hold back tears)
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, tears welling up in eyes) Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up. Even when the baby is sleeping, I'll lie awake at night, just thinking about everything that's been going on, and feeling really overwhelmed and unhappy. (sighing) It's like, my mind just won't turn off, and I'll be thinking about all the things I need to do, or worrying about the baby, or just feeling really down and sad. (looking down) And then, when I do finally fall asleep, I'll have these really vivid dreams that are just so... unsettling. (shuddering) They're not always bad dreams, but they're just really intense, and they'll leave me feeling really anxious and on edge. (rubbing eyes) And then, of course, I'll wake up feeling exhausted, because I haven't gotten a good night's sleep. (sighing) It's just this vicious cycle, you know? I'll be tired, so I'll feel overwhelmed, and then I'll worry about everything, and that'll keep me up at night... (trailing off, shaking head) It's just really hard to break out of that cycle, you know? (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) I just feel like I'm so tired, all the time, and I don't know how to make it stop.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, tears streaming down face) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I just feel so... sad and miserable, all the time. It's like, I'll be doing something, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of sadness wash over me, and I'll start crying. (sobbing) It's not even always about anything specific, it's just this feeling of... (searching for words) ...of emptiness, I guess. Like, I'm just going through the motions of being a mom, but I'm not really feeling anything. (looking down) And it's hard, because I feel like I should be happy, you know? I've got a beautiful baby, and a loving partner, and a comfortable home... (shaking head) But none of that seems to matter, when I'm feeling this way. (sighing) It's like, I'm just trapped in this fog of sadness, and I don't know how to get out of it. (looking up, eyes red and puffy) Sometimes, I'll be holding the baby, and I'll just feel this overwhelming sense of sadness, and I'll think to myself, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I just be happy?" (voice cracking) It's like, I'm failing at being a mom, and I'm failing at being a person... (trailing off, overcome with emotion)
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears streaming down face) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I just feel like I'm crying all the time. (sobbing) It's not even always about anything specific, it's just this feeling of... (searching for words) ...of overwhelm, I guess. Like, I'll be doing something, and suddenly I'll just feel this wave of emotion wash over me, and I'll start crying. (looking down) And it's not just little tears, either. I'm talking about full-on, sobbing, can't-catch-my-breath crying. (shaking head) It's like, my body just takes over, and I'm powerless to stop it. (sighing) And it's hard, because I feel like I should be able to control my emotions, you know? I'm a mom now, and I'm supposed to be strong and capable... (looking up, eyes red and puffy) But the truth is, I'm just not feeling that way right now. (voice cracking) I'm feeling weak, and scared, and just really, really overwhelmed. (trailing off, overcome with emotion)

(pauses, taking a deep breath) I think it's been about once or twice a week, lately. I'll just be doing something, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of emotion wash over me, and I'll start crying. (shaking head) It's not always because of anything specific, it's just... (sighing) I don't know, it's just everything, I guess. Being a new mom, and trying to figure everything out, and just feeling so... (searching for words) ...so lost, I guess. (looking down) Yeah, that's it. I just feel lost, and alone, and really, really scared. (voice cracking) And the crying just feels like the only way to release all of that emotion, you know? (trailing off, overcome with emotion)
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pauses, looking down, voice barely above a whisper) Yes... I have had those thoughts. (pausing again, struggling to find the words) It's not like I want to hurt myself, or that I'm planning to do anything... (shaking head) It's just that sometimes, when I'm feeling really overwhelmed and sad, the thought will just... (pausing once more) ...pop into my head. (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) And it's scary, because I don't know where it's coming from, or why I'm thinking it. (voice cracking) I just feel like I'm not in control, and that's really frightening.

(taking a deep breath, trying to compose herself) I think it's happened a few times, over the past week or so. (pausing, struggling to find the words) It's just this fleeting thought, you know? Like, "What if I just...?" (trailing off, not finishing the sentence) And then I'll just push it away, and try to focus on something else. (looking down, shame and fear in her eyes) I don't know why I'm having these thoughts, or what's causing them... (pausing, searching for words) I just know that they're there, and that they're scaring me.

(looking up, tears streaming down her face) I don't want to hurt myself, I swear. (voice cracking) I just want to be a good mom, and take care of my baby... (sobbing) And I don't know why these thoughts are happening, or how to make them stop. (trailing off, overcome with emotion)

As a new mother, you're experiencing a range of emotions and challenges that are common during the postpartum period. It takes a lot of courage to acknowledge and share your feelings, and I'm here to support you. Your feelings of sadness, anxiety, and overwhelm are valid, and it's essential to address them to ensure your well-being and ability to care for your baby.

thoughts, matching the 'Yes, very often' option.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, quite a lot' option</sym>, <sym>the option 'Yes, most of the time I haven't been able to cope at all</sym>, <sym>The patient's baby.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates that they have been crying frequently, describing it as 'a lot lately' and 'about once or twice a week', with intense emotional episodes of 'full-on, sobbing, can't-catch-my-breath crying', which aligns with the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient mentions having thoughts of harming herself 'a few times, over the past week or so' and describes them as 'fleeting thoughts' that she tries to push away, which aligns with the 'Sometimes' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's responses indicate a high level of distress and symptomatology consistent with <med>Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>. The EPDS score of 28 suggests a probable depression, and the presence of suicidal thoughts necessitates urgent referral to a <med>primary care provider</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>. The patient's symptoms, including <sym>sadness</sym>, <sym>anxiety</sym>, <sym>panic</sym>, <sym>guilt</sym>, and <sym>worthlessness</sym>, are consistent with <med>DSM-5 criteria</med> for <med>Major Depressive Disorder</med>. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>primary care provider</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Discuss <med>postpartum depression</med> treatment options, including <med>psychotherapy</med> and <med>medication</med>
3. Encourage <med>sleep hygiene practices</med> and <med>relaxation techniques</med> to manage <sym>anxiety</sym> and <sym>stress</sym>
4. Provide resources for <med>postpartum support groups</med> and <med>online counseling services</med>
5. Emphasize the importance of <med>self-care</med> and <med>social support</med> during the postpartum period

postpartum depression screening impression for patient with EPDS score 28: **Postpartum Depression Screening Summary**

The patient presents with a range of symptoms and emotional concerns that warrant further evaluation. Key symptoms and patterns observed during the screening include:

* Persistent feelings of sadness, loss of pleasure, and enjoyment in activities
* Difficulty sleeping, with sleep disturbances linked to mood and anxiety
* Overwhelming feelings of guilt, worthlessness, and self-doubt regarding mothering abilities
* Significant anxiety, panic, and feelings of being overwhelmed, particularly in relation to the baby's care and well-being
* Recurrent crying spells, occurring approximately once or twice a week, in response to feelings of emotional overload

Notable risk factors identified during the screening include:

* Persistent sadness and loss of pleasure
* Sleep difficulties linked to mood
* Feelings of worthlessness and guilt
* Anxiety, panic, and being overwhelmed
* **Safety concern:** The patient has reported fleeting thoughts of self-harm, which requires immediate attention and follow-up.

The patient's responses suggest a pattern of emotional and behavioral concerns that may be indicative of postpartum depression and/or anxiety. The presence of suicidal thoughts is a significant safety concern that necessitates prompt evaluation and intervention.

**Recommendations:**

* Further evaluation and assessment to determine the severity and scope of symptoms
* Immediate follow-up to address safety concerns and provide support
* Consideration of referral to a mental health specialist for comprehensive evaluation and treatment planning

This screening summary is intended to inform further clinical evaluation and guide the development of a treatment plan. It is not a formal diagnosis, and a comprehensive diagnostic assessment is necessary to determine the presence and severity of any mental health conditions.
